historical_record.description: The deed recorded here set a floor of $2,500 on the house to be built — one of the building restrictions the Parkside Realty Company borrowed from the residence parks. The permit taken out for the construction put its value at $1,500. W. E. Collins was the architect.

One of the houses in the district that predate the stucco “Sunset” row house which filled the Parkside from the 1920s — mostly larger Craftsman-style buildings put up by the Parkside Realty Company before 1925.

building.completed_conflict: The Parkside context statement records the deed conditions and the construction permit for the house here in 1920; the assessor dates the building on this parcel to 1918.

unknowns: The 1920 deed conditions for this house required a building costing at least $2,500, while the permit taken out for the construction put its value at $1,500. Which figure the finished building answered to is not recorded.
